title: Japanese immigration and nationality law for long-term resident status of Japanese descent

laws.title: Ministry of Justice Notice No. 132 of 1990 (teijusha notice), the positions of long-term resident status set in advance under art. 7(1)(ii) of the Immigration Control Act, items 1 to 8
laws.amendment: Amended by further Ministry of Justice notices; the texts read give no schedule. It is not on e-Gov; the Immigration Services Agency publishes a consolidated copy whose heading names the latest amendment, Notice No. 220 of 2021-10-28, and its page on the notice gives the same latest amendment and the original date, 1990-05-24. The notice has applied since 1990-06-01; item 2 is deleted.

laws.title: Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951): arts. 2, 2-2, 5, 5-2, 7, 7-2, 19, 20, 21, 22-2, 22-4 and 67, appended table II
laws.amendment: Though issued as a 1951 Cabinet Order it is amended by Acts of the Diet, several times a year, often in stages. e-Gov shows the text in force from 2026-10-01 (Act No. 32 of 2026, whose fee stage began then) and versions not yet in force for 2027-04-01 (Act No. 60 of 2024) and for 2027-03-31 (Act No. 39 of 2025), 2028-10-31 and 2029-03-31 (Act No. 32 of 2026); those last 3 are only the latest days the acts allow, and a Cabinet Order sets the real day. Appended table II and art. 5 read the same in the 2029-03-31 version.

laws.title: Ordinance for Enforcement of the Immigration Control Act (Ministry of Justice Ordinance No. 54 of 1981): art. 6-2, appended table 2 (periods of stay), tables 3 and 4 (documents and agents)
laws.amendment: Amended by Ministry of Justice ordinances, often several times a year (in 2026 on 2026-03-31, 2026-04-01, 2026-05-21, 2026-06-14, 2026-07-01, 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01). e-Gov lists amendments not yet in force for 2027-03-19 (Ordinance No. 43 of 2025) and 2027-04-01 (Ordinance No. 45 of 2025).

laws.title: Order for Enforcement of the Immigration Control Act (Cabinet Order No. 178 of 1998): art. 25, fees for change of status, extension of stay and re-entry
laws.amendment: Amended by Cabinet Orders. The fee schedule in art. 25 was rewritten by Cabinet Order No. 268 of 2026 from 2026-10-01, the day the art. 67 amendment of Act No. 32 of 2026 took effect; fees change only when the Cabinet amends this order, within the caps of art. 67 of the act. e-Gov lists a version for 2027-04-01 (Cabinet Order No. 341 of 2025).

laws.title: Ministry of Justice Ordinance No. 16 of 1990 setting the standards of art. 7(1)(ii) of the Immigration Control Act
laws.amendment: Amended by Ministry of Justice ordinances, once or twice a year since 2022 (last 2026-04-01, Ordinance No. 12 of 2026); e-Gov lists an amendment for 2027-04-01 (Ordinance No. 45 of 2025). It sets standards only for activities of appended table I, parts 2 and 4, and has no row for long-term residents.

laws.title: Nationality Act (Act No. 147 of 1950): arts. 2, 3, 11 to 15, and the supplementary provisions of the original Act and of Act No. 45 of 1984
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the Diet, rarely; the last were Act No. 59 of 2018 (2022-04-01), Act No. 68 of 2022 (2022-06-17 and 2025-06-01) and Act No. 102 of 2022 (2024-04-01), each with transitional rules in its supplementary provisions. e-Gov lists no amendment scheduled, and its oldest version is of 2015-04-01. In force since 1950-07-01, when it repealed the Nationality Act of 1899 (Act No. 66 of 1899), which is not on e-Gov.

laws.title: Civil Code (Act No. 89 of 1896): art. 4 (majority at 18), arts. 140 to 143 (periods), arts. 731, 739, 779, 784, 792, 798, 809 and 817-2 to 817-9 (marriage, recognition, adoption)
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the Diet, each with its own commencement and transitional provisions in its supplementary provisions. Majority moved from 20 to 18 on 2022-04-01 (Act No. 59 of 2018). e-Gov shows the text of 2026-06-24 (Act No. 45 of 2026) and versions for 2027-06-23, 2027-12-05, 2028-06-13, 2028-12-23 and 2029-06-23, dates that are the latest the amending acts allow or follow another act's commencement, so they may still move; in the 2029 version arts. 4, 143, 731, 739, 784 and 809 read the same.

laws.title: Act on the Calculation of Age (Act No. 50 of 1902): age counts from the day of birth, applying Civil Code art. 143
laws.amendment: e-Gov lists a single version, dated 1902-12-22, with no amendment. It has 2 operative rules and a repeal of Proclamation No. 36 of 1873, and borrows its method from Civil Code art. 143, so a change to art. 143 changes how age is counted.

laws.title: Act on General Rules for Application of Laws (Act No. 78 of 2006): arts. 4, 24, 28, 29, 31 and 38, the law that governs capacity, marriage, parentage and adoption
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the Diet, rarely: e-Gov lists the original text in force from 2007-01-01 and 1 amendment, Act No. 46 of 2026, in force from 2026-06-24, with a further stage dated 2028-12-23, tied to the commencement of Act No. 45 of 2026, that leaves arts. 4, 24, 28, 29, 31 and 38 as they are.

pitfalls.text: Appended table II gives long-term resident status to a person the Minister permits to reside for a set period for special reasons, but art. 7(1)(ii) limits landing to the positions the Minister sets in advance by notice, so for a newcomer the notice sets which positions qualify; passport, visa and refusal grounds still apply (art. 7(1)). The landing-standards ordinance covers only activities of appended table I, parts 2 and 4, so it sets no income, language or job threshold. The enforcement ordinance also gives periods for positions outside the notice, up to 5 years set case by case.

The notice is not on e-Gov; a title search there finds nothing. The only pinned text is the Immigration Services Agency's consolidated copy, headed with its latest amendment, Notice No. 220 of 2021-10-28, and carrying no date of its own. An amendment newer than the copy would not show in it; the agency's page on the notice also names the latest amendment (最近改正).

Item 3 needs a biological child of a person born as a child of a Japanese national, so it turns on the grandparent's nationality on the parent's birth date. Item 4 needs a biological grandchild of a person who was born as a child of a Japanese national and once had a family register in Japan as a Japanese national, so it turns on the great-grandparent's nationality at the grandparent's birth and on the grandparent's register. Item 4 excludes anyone under item 3; both exclude items 1 and 8. The notice uses no generation labels.

Item 3 asks how the parent was born, not whether the parent is or was Japanese. The 1984 amendment of the Nationality Act (Act No. 45 of 1984, in force 1985-01-01) let those born from 1965-01-01 to 1984-12-31 who were not Japanese, whose mother was Japanese at the birth and still is or was at her death, acquire nationality by notification within 3 years, from the notification (supplementary art. 5), so before 1985 a child of a Japanese mother was not always Japanese. Such a parent was still born as a child of a Japanese national.

Items 3 and 4 need biological child (jisshi) links from the principal up to the person born as a child of a Japanese national, so an adopted link does not count, though under Civil Code art. 809 an adoptee takes the status of the adopter's legitimate child. A recognition takes effect from the birth under Civil Code art. 784, while Nationality Act art. 3 gives a recognized child nationality only from the notification; the notice does not say whether a child recognized after birth was born as a child of a Japanese national.

The line turns on an ancestor's nationality on a past birth date, under the text in force then. Today a Japanese national loses it on acquiring a foreign nationality by choice or choosing one under foreign law (art. 11), and one born abroad with a foreign nationality from birth loses it back to the birth unless it was reserved under the Family Register Act (art. 12). Earlier wording differed: Act No. 45 of 1984 (from 1985-01-01), supplementary art. 4, refers to loss under the former art. 9, and e-Gov has no version before 2015. The 1899 Act, repealed from 1950-07-01, is not on e-Gov.

Statuses of residence are for foreigners, defined in art. 2(i) of the act as anyone without Japanese nationality, so a dual national who still holds Japanese nationality cannot take this status. Missing the choice deadline of Nationality Act art. 14 (age 20, or 2 years after becoming dual after 18; those dual and 20 or older on 2022-04-01 keep the former rule, Act No. 59 of 2018, supplementary art. 13(2)) does not by itself end it: under art. 15 the Minister may demand a choice in writing, and nationality is lost if none is made in 1 month. Renunciation is effective at notification (art. 13).

A person in Japan who gives up Japanese nationality becomes a foreigner at the notification and may stay without a status for 60 days, but must apply to acquire a status within 30 days to stay longer (art. 22-2 of the act).

The spouse (item 5(c)) qualifies through someone already holding long-term resident status under item 3 or 4 with a period of stay of 1 year or more, minor children (item 6(c)) through such a holder or through a spouse holding the status under item 5(c), and adopted children (item 7(c)) through any long-term resident with 1 year or more. For notice positions the periods are 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 6 months, so a holder granted 6 months anchors no family member. The period is set at the grant, so before the grant the texts do not settle whether a holder anchors a family member.

For an item 3 or 4 holder, items 5 to 7 list the spouse of good conduct; minor, unmarried biological children whom the holder supports and who are of good conduct; and adopted children under 6 whom the holder supports, with no good-conduct or marriage condition. Parents, siblings, adult children and older adoptees are not listed. Items 6(c) and 7 speak of these persons' children supported by these persons, which leaves open whose support counts for a stepchild, or for the holder's own child supported by the spouse.

The notice says minor without an age. Civil Code art. 4 sets majority at 18 from 2022-04-01 (Act No. 59 of 2018); before that it was 20, and those aged 18 or 19 on that day became adults on it. Act on General Rules art. 4 governs a person's capacity by their national law, and the notice does not say whether minor follows it or the Civil Code. The notice gives no reference date for minor or under 6.

Age counts from the day of birth by Civil Code art. 143, under the Act on the Calculation of Age. A year counted from the birth day ends at the end of the day before the anniversary, so a person reaches each age at the end of the day before the birthday. For a birthday on 29 February, art. 143(2) ends the year at the end of February, so in common years the new age counts from 1 March.

The notice does not define spouse. Under Act on General Rules art. 24 the formation of a marriage follows each party's national law, and its form the law of the place of celebration or either party's national law, except that a marriage celebrated in Japan with a Japanese party cannot rely on the other party's national form. Whether a foreign marriage counts is a question under these rules.

Good conduct in items 3, 4, 5(c) and 6(c) is not defined and sits on top of the landing refusal grounds of art. 5(1), which include a sentence of imprisonment of 1 year or more under any country's law, except for political crimes; any sentence under drug laws; risk of becoming a public charge; and a bar of 1, 5 or 10 years after deportation or a departure order. Art. 5-2 lets the Minister overlook some of these grounds in cases set by ordinance.

A person born as a child of a Japanese national has their own status, spouse or child of Japanese national, in appended table II, and the spouse of a holder of that status who was born as a child of a Japanese national comes under item 5(a). Item 1 (persons staying in named Asian countries whom the UN refugee agency recommends to Japan for protection) and item 8 (Japanese left in China and their families) are separate positions of the notice.

Art. 19 limits paid work only for appended table I statuses, so it puts no work limit on a long-term resident. Revocation under art. 22-4 for not pursuing an activity (items 5 and 6) also applies only to table I, but the grounds for false documents and for not reporting an address within 90 days apply. From 2027-04-01 (Act No. 60 of 2024) art. 22-4 adds new items 8 and 9 for permanent residents, and the address grounds move from items 8 to 10 to items 10 to 12.

From 2026-10-01 the fee for a change of status or an extension depends on the period granted, up to JPY 75,000 for 5 years or more (JPY 65,000 online), against JPY 6,000 before; art. 67 caps it at JPY 100,000 and lists no fee for a certificate of eligibility or for landing. Applications filed before that day keep the old fee (Act No. 32 of 2026, supplementary art. 5).

For a long-term resident the ordinance asks, at landing, a certificate of eligibility, or a change or acquisition of status (appended table 3), documents proving personal status such as family register copies and marriage and birth certificates, proof that the costs of the stay can be paid or of the payer's income, and a letter from a guarantor living in Japan; at an extension (table 3-7), the same status documents and guarantor, with proof of income and tax paid or of the supporter's income. A relative living in Japan may apply for the certificate as agent (table 4).

e-Gov holds versions of the act, the order, the ordinances, the Civil Code and the Act on General Rules that are not in force yet, several dated only by the latest day their amending act allows. The version in force on a given date, not the newest, holds the law for that date. By its 2029-03-31 version the act rewords art. 7(1)(iii), adds in art. 7(1)(v) an authorization for visa-exempt short stays under a new art. 7-2, and moves the certificate of eligibility to art. 7-3, but art. 5, art. 7(1)(ii) and appended table II stay unchanged.
